# `silk/json_reader`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Profiles: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`.

Allocation-free JSON token reading from a fixed-capacity buffered input.

## When to use

Use [`JsonReader`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6a736f6e5f7265616465723a3a4a736f6e526561646572) when a JSON document does not fit in one input slice. Use
`silk.json_scanner.JsonScanner` when the complete document is available.

## Details

Each call to [`next`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6a736f6e5f7265616465723a3a4a736f6e5265616465722e6e657874) returns one validated token. Raw string, number, and literal bytes use
caller-owned scratch storage. The reader keeps no input or scratch view between calls.

## Gotchas

A raw token longer than scratch fails with `JsonReason.TokenTooLarge`. The reader becomes
terminal after a JSON, buffer, or capacity failure. Drop each token view before the next call.

Import as `JsonReader` with `import silk.json_reader { JsonReader }`.

Public declarations: 2.

## `JsonReadToken`

```silk
pub struct JsonReadToken<'scratch>
```

One validated token and its raw bytes in caller-owned scratch storage.

### Details

`raw` includes quotes and escapes for strings. Punctuation and end-of-input have an empty
`raw` slice. The view remains valid only while its scratch borrow is held.

## `JsonReader`

```silk
pub struct JsonReader
```

Owned state for one JSON document read from `BufferedInput`.

### Details

This state keeps no input or scratch reference. It retains scanner progress across input
fills. A completed document returns sticky end-of-input.

<a id="declaration-73696c6b2f6a736f6e5f7265616465723a3a4a736f6e5265616465722e6d616b65"></a>

### Method `JsonReader.next`

```silk
pub effect<'scratch & 'life1 & 'life2> fn next<'scratch, 'life1, 'life2>(self: &'life1 mut silk/json_reader.JsonReader, input: &'life2 mut silk/buffered_input.BufferedInput, scratch: &'scratch mut [u8], deadline: silk/option.Option<silk/system_clock.Instant>) -> silk/json_reader.JsonReadToken<'scratch> ! JsonError | BufferError ? &mut ByteDuplex | &mut MonotonicClock
```

Returns the next token with raw bytes copied into caller scratch.

#### Details

The token view borrows only `scratch`. A number at an input boundary waits for its delimiter.
The delimiter stays in `input` for the next call. Whitespace uses no scratch space.

#### Gotchas

If scratch is too small, `JsonReason.TokenTooLarge` reports the token's first byte and the
available capacity. JSON and buffer failures also make the reader terminal. End is sticky.
